body.statement: Theorem 3.15 of Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal is false as written. Let \(G_{\times}=\{1\to2,2\to3,3\to4,1\to3\}\), let \(G_{\mathrm{ch}}=\{1\to2,2\to3,3\to4\}\), and consider \(j=1\), so \(C_1=\{2\}\) and \(R_1=\{3,4\}\). With \(\alpha=\Lambda^{(0)}_{21}\), \(b=\Lambda^{(0)}_{32}\), \(d=\Lambda^{(0)}_{31}\), \(\beta=\delta_{32}\), \(\delta=\delta_{31}\), and \(\gamma=\delta_{43}\), the two actual-row rank matrices derived from Equation (20) are \[M_{G_{\times},G_{\mathrm{ch}}}[1]=H[\{3,4\},\{2\}]=\begin{pmatrix}\beta\\ \gamma b\end{pmatrix},\qquad \bigl(M_{G_{\times},G_{\mathrm{ch}}}[1]\mid b_{G_{\times},G_{\mathrm{ch}}}[1]\bigr)=H[\{3,4\},\{2,1\}]=\begin{pmatrix}\beta&\delta+\alpha\beta\\ \gamma b&\gamma(d+\alpha b)\end{pmatrix}.\] The augmented determinant is \(\gamma(\beta d-b\delta)\). It is not the zero polynomial: \(\alpha=b=c=d=\beta=\gamma=1\), \(\delta=2\), and \(\delta_{21}=1\) give value \(-1\), while every true edge and every intervention change is nonzero and each changed coefficient is retained. Hence it is nonzero on a relative Zariski-open subset allowed by Assumption 1.2 and the exact-support and retained-edge conditions, where the two ranks are \(1\) and \(2\). The specialization \((\beta,\delta)=(b,d)\) used in the proof of Theorem 3.15 identifies independent parameter variables and changes the determinant to \(\gamma(bd-bd)=0\), dropping the augmented rank to \(1\). Thus \(G_{\mathrm{ch}}\in\mathsf H_{\mathrm{obs}}(G_{\times})\) but \(G_{\mathrm{ch}}\notin\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G_{\times})\) on \(\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{term},p,4}(G_{\times},G_{\mathrm{ch}})\), throughout the positive-variance ambient domain.
body.justification: The explicit indexed matrices isolate the invalid generic-rank substitution and prove that the corrected graph class differs on an admissible open set.
body.gap: The proof of Theorem 3.15 first uses the correct actual \(\Delta^{(k)}\) rows, then replaces each independent change \(\lambda^{(k)}_{ki}-\lambda^{(0)}_{ki}\) by \(\lambda^{(0)}_{ki}\) while claiming generic rank is preserved; the displayed minor proves that this nongeneric specialization can lower rank.
body.consumer: This is a Problem 5.1 regression test preventing the LCD workflow from certifying a chain that violates the actual changed mechanism rows.
body.proof_tex:
The two graphs have the same transitive closure, namely the total reachability order \(1<2<3<4\).  For \(G_{\mathrm{ch}}\) and \(j=1\), one has \(C_1=\{2\}\) and \(R_1=\{3,4\}\).  In \(G_\times\), path expansion of \(P=(I_4-\Lambda^{(0)})^{-1}\) gives
\[
 P[\{3,4\},\{2,1\}]
 =\begin{pmatrix}
 b&d+\alpha b\\
 cb&c(d+\alpha b)
 \end{pmatrix}.
\]
Its second row is \(c\) times its first row.  Since \(b\ne0\), both \(P[\{3,4\},\{2\}]\) and the displayed augmented matrix have rank one.  The other baseline tests also pass: for \(j=2\), \(C_2=\{3\}\), \(R_2=\{4\}\), and the row \((P_{43},P_{42})=(c,cb)\) has the same rank as its first entry; for \(j=3,4\), the relevant nonchild-descendant sets are empty.  Therefore \(G_{\mathrm{ch}}\in\mathsf H_{\mathrm{obs}}(G_\times)\).

The actual intervention rows are obtained from \(h_k^{\mathsf T}=\delta_k^{\mathsf T}P\).  At targets three and four this gives
\[
 h_3^{\mathsf T}=(\delta+\alpha\beta,\beta,0,0),
 \qquad
 h_4^{\mathsf T}=(\gamma(d+\alpha b),\gamma b,\gamma,0).
\]
Hence
\[
 H[\{3,4\},\{2\}]
 =\begin{pmatrix}\beta\\ \gamma b\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 H[\{3,4\},\{2,1\}]
 =\begin{pmatrix}
 \beta&\delta+\alpha\beta\\
 \gamma b&\gamma(d+\alpha b)
 \end{pmatrix},
\]
and
\[
 \det H[\{3,4\},\{2,1\}]
 =\gamma\{\beta(d+\alpha b)-b(\delta+\alpha\beta)\}
 =\gamma(\beta d-b\delta).
\]
This polynomial is nonzero: at \(\alpha=b=c=d=\beta=\gamma=1\) and \(\delta=2\) it equals \(-1\).  Taking also \(\delta_{21}=1\), the post-change edge coefficients are \(2\) on \(1\to2\), \(2\) on \(2\to3\), \(3\) on \(1\to3\), and \(2\) on \(3\to4\).  Thus every baseline edge, every required change, and every retained edge is nonzero.  The nonvanishing determinant persists on a nonempty relative Zariski-open subset, which meets \(\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{term},p,4}(G_\times,G_{\mathrm{ch}})\).  On that subset the unaugmented rank is one and the augmented rank is two, so the affine system for column one is inconsistent.  The terminal-certificate theorem therefore gives \(G_{\mathrm{ch}}\notin\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G_\times)\).

If one makes the specialization \((\beta,\delta)=(b,d)\), the same determinant becomes \(\gamma(bd-bd)=0\).  Since \((\beta,\delta)\) are intervention-change coordinates while \((b,d)\) are baseline-edge coordinates, exact support and retention impose only nonvanishing conditions and do not justify these two equalities.  The specialization therefore lies on a proper algebraic subset and can reduce generic rank.  No variance entered the calculation, so the mismatch holds throughout the positive-variance ambient domain.
